topic: Types of Variables and Data in Experiments
key_concepts: Independent variable is the factor changed or manipulated in an experiment.
Dependent variable is the factor measured or observed in response to the independent varia
Controlled variables are kept constant across experimental set-ups.
Keeping other factors constant isolates the effect of the independent variable.
Quantitative data are obtained by counting or measuring.
Qualitative data are descriptive and involve characteristics not usually counted.
Scientists organize data using tables, charts, and graphs.
In plant growth experiments, amount of light or soil type can be independent variables.
Plant height, number of leaves, and leaf condition can be dependent variables.
Tables help organize and analyze experimental data.
Average score is calculated by summing values and dividing by the number of values.
